note: RR-264: every fact the ten new pages use, recorded ONCE (one sentence, one claim, one tier-1 source each) and reused by every page that needs it; and every read that found no answer. Read 14 October 2026 by research agents of actor:cc, public pages only, no login.

facts.sourceName: OET help centre — How much does the OET Test cost?
facts.text: OET lists the full four-part test at AU$587 (US$455 for the computer test or OET@Home taken in the USA).
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page lists AU$587 for the full test and US$455 in the USA; no rupee amount appears

facts.sourceName: OET help centre — How much does the OET Test cost?
facts.text: Booking one, two or three sub-tests again on paper at a venue costs AU$315, AU$415 or AU$515, each including a AU$7 booking fee.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page lists the single sub-test fees for the paper test

facts.sourceName: OET — The OET Test
facts.text: Listening and Reading are the same for every profession, while Writing and Speaking are set in the candidate's own profession.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the overview marks Listening and Reading as common and Writing and Speaking as profession-specific

facts.sourceName: OET — Writing sub-test
facts.text: The Writing sub-test takes 45 minutes, starting with 5 minutes of reading time, and asks for a formal letter based on case notes from the candidate's profession.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives 45 minutes with 5 of reading time and a profession-specific letter from case notes

facts.sourceName: OET — Speaking sub-test
facts.text: The Speaking sub-test takes about 20 minutes and is made of two role-plays of 5 minutes each, set in the candidate's own profession.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives about 20 minutes and two profession-specific role-plays of 5 minutes

facts.sourceName: OET — Results and scoring
facts.text: Each OET sub-test is scored from 0 to 500 and given a grade from A to E, and a score of 350 is a grade B.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives the 0 to 500 scale, grades A to E and B = 350

facts.sourceName: OET — Results and scoring
facts.text: OET aims to release computer-test and OET@Home results within 6 calendar days of the last sub-test.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page states a 6-calendar-day aim (met in 95% of cases) for the computer test and OET@Home

facts.sourceName: OET — Results and scoring
facts.text: Paper-test results can be released 12 days after the test date.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives 12 days for the paper test

facts.sourceName: OET — Results and scoring
facts.text: OET sets no validity period of its own: each regulator or organisation that accepts OET decides how old a result may be.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page leaves validity to the recognising body

facts.sourceName: OET — Book a test
facts.text: A test is booked on OET's own website by searching for a test near you and choosing the computer test at a venue, OET@Home or the paper test.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives the search-and-book route and the three formats

facts.sourceName: OET — Book a test
facts.text: Bookings close 24 days before the test date for the paper test and 7 days before for the computer test and OET@Home.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives the 24-day and 7-day closing rules

facts.sourceName: OET — Test regulations
facts.text: On test day OET accepts a valid passport or a national identity card showing your name, photo and date of birth, and it must be the document you booked with.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the regulations list passport and national ID with these conditions

facts.sourceName: OET help centre — Can I defer/reschedule my OET Test to a different date?
facts.text: A computer-test or OET@Home booking can be moved up to two days before the first sub-test, for AU$120 before bookings close or AU$200 after.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives the two-day limit and the AU$120 and AU$200 fees

facts.sourceName: OET — Speaking sub-test available at a venue for select countries
facts.text: OET's website names Islamabad, Karachi and Lahore as the cities in Pakistan where computer-test candidates can take the Speaking sub-test at a venue.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page's list of places has Pakistan with Islamabad, Karachi and Lahore

facts.sourceName: Ahpra — Accepted English language tests
facts.text: For an OET sat on or after 23 April 2026, Ahpra's National Boards ask for at least 350 in Listening, 360 in Reading, 350 in Writing and 360 in Speaking.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives these per-component minimums and no overall score; the same list applies to every National Board but one

facts.body: HCPC (Health and Care Professions Council, UK)
facts.sourceName: HCPC — English language proficiency
facts.text: HCPC accepts the OET in the applicant's own profession with an overall score of at least 1400 and no sub-test below 300.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives 1400 overall and 300 per sub-test for these professions (1800 and 400 only for speech and language therapists)

facts.sourceName: CORU — Language requirements
facts.text: CORU asks for the OET with grade B (350) in three components and at least C+ (300) in the fourth.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page's table gives B x3 and C+ x1 for physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, podiatrists and optometrists

facts.sourceName: CORU — Language requirements
facts.text: CORU asks radiographers for the OET with at least grade B (350) in all four components.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page's table gives grade B in all four for radiographers

facts.sourceName: Medical Council of Ireland — English language requirements
facts.text: The Medical Council of Ireland accepts the OET only in Medicine, with at least grade B in every sub-test gained in one sitting.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives Medicine only, grade B each, one sitting

facts.sourceName: Medical Council of New Zealand — English language policy
facts.text: The Medical Council of New Zealand asks doctors for at least 350 in Speaking, Listening and Reading and 300 in Writing in the OET Medicine.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the policy gives 350/350/350 and 300 in Writing

facts.sourceName: General Dental Council — Guidance on English language controls
facts.text: Where the General Dental Council asks a dentist to sit an English test, it names IELTS Academic, and its guidance does not name the OET.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the guidance names IELTS Academic (6.5 each, 7 overall) and no other test

facts.sourceName: Dental Council (NZ) — English language
facts.text: The Dental Council of New Zealand asks for an OET pass with grade A or B in all four components, valid for two years.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives A or B in each component and two years

facts.sourceName: Dental Council of Ireland — Language proficiency
facts.text: The Dental Council of Ireland asks for the OET in Dentistry with at least grade B in each of the four modules.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives grade B in each module

facts.sourceName: Pharmacy Council of New Zealand — English language requirements
facts.text: The Pharmacy Council of New Zealand asks for grade A or B in each OET sub-test, gained within two years of applying.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives A or B in each band within two years

facts.sourceName: PSI — Language requirements
facts.text: The Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland accepts the OET for pharmacist registration, and a result stays valid for two years from the test date.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page lists OET among accepted tests and gives two years from the test date (its score table is not used: two of its rows disagree)

facts.sourceName: General Optical Council — International optometrists
facts.text: The General Optical Council accepts only IELTS as an English test for international optometrists, so the OET is not accepted.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page names IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI Academic only

facts.body: Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Board (New Zealand)
facts.sourceName: ODOB — English language requirements (policy)
facts.text: The Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Board asks for at least grade B (350) in each of the four OET components in one result.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the policy gives B (350) in each component, one result

facts.body: Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand
facts.sourceName: Occupational Therapy Board of NZ — Overseas applicants
facts.text: The Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand accepts the OET as proof of English for applicants whose first language is not English.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page names OET or IELTS; the grades are in a policy document that could not be read

facts.sourceName: Dietitians Australia — Skills recognition, English language
facts.text: Dietitians Australia asks overseas-qualified dietitians for at least 350 (grade B) in each of the four OET components.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives 350 (B) in each component

facts.sourceName: Dietitians Board — English language requirements
facts.text: The Dietitians Board of New Zealand asks for grade A or B in all four OET sections, dated within the 12 months before it receives the application.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives A or B in all four and 12 months

facts.sourceName: RCVS — English language requirements
facts.text: The RCVS asks for the OET in Veterinary Science with an overall grade B, at least B in three sub-tests and no lower than C+ in the fourth.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page gives overall B, B in three and C+ minimum

facts.sourceName: Veterinary Council of NZ — English competence policy
facts.text: The Veterinary Council of New Zealand asks for grade A or B in each of the four OET sub-tests, all from one sitting.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the policy gives A or B in each and one sitting

facts.sourceName: AVBC — English language standards
facts.text: The Australasian Veterinary Boards Council accepts English test results only from tests sat in person, so OET@Home is not accepted.
facts.whatSupportsIt: the page accepts in-person tests only
